Across Viewpoints and Time:
Trajectory-Generalizable Physical Attacks on

Song Xia1, Meiewen Ding1, Chenqi Kong2, Wenhan Yang3, Xudong Jiang1

1 Nanyang Technological University2 National University of Singapore3 Pengcheng Lab

Paper Code Videos

Motivation. In physical deployment, a patch moves with its supporting surface rather than staying fixed on screen. Changes in viewpoint, scale, and occlusion must therefore be handled throughout a video, not just in a single image.

Research objective. TARA learns a single adversarial texture that stays attached to an object and remains effective across different videos, viewpoints, and observation trajectories.

Align first. Refine for the task.

Heterogeneous videos and trajectories produce conflicting texture gradients. TARA builds a more compatible starting point for shared optimization.

01

Render along a trajectory

Attach one canonical texture to a surface. Frame-wise homographies and visibility masks account for motion, perspective, and occlusion.

γi = {(Hit, Mit)}t=1T
02

Align attacked representations

Bring attacked features from different video–trajectory instances toward a shared region, while separating them from their own clean features.

Lcon = meani≠j softplus[(s(zia, zic) − s(zia, zja)) / τ]
03

Refine toward prediction errors

Optimize the aggregated task prediction from the aligned texture. Visibility-aware weights balance texture exposure; generation refinement targets reconstruction error.

Lref = Σi wi log pθ(yi | X̃i(δ; γi))

Main results

We evaluate action anticipation on EK100, action recognition on SSV2, and future frame generation with DiLA.

Top-1 ASR is conditioned on clean-correct predictions. Avg. is the mean across models.

Generalization beyond training observations

Frozen textures under independent changes in content and observation trajectory.

TARAEOT

Top-1 ASR (%), V-JEPA2-L on EK100. Each condition uses 74 clip instances; unseen content comes from 35 independently captured recordings.

Trajectory benchmark

We annotate surface homographies and visibility masks on EK100 and SSV2, and collect real-world print-and-capture videos. Fixed trajectories allow different textures to be compared under the same geometry and visibility.
